questions.question: What is the main point of the First Truth in this passage?
questions.answer: It teaches that only Allah truly deserves worship.

questions.question: What are some things in the universe that lead people to worship and thank Allah?
questions.answer: The many blessings and gifts people receive lead them to praise, thank, and worship Allah.

questions.question: How do animals and even nonliving things show a kind of worship in the passage?
questions.answer: They do it by carrying out the jobs and purposes given to them.

questions.question: What do revelation, inspiration, and unseen spiritual signs all agree on?
questions.answer: They all point to Allah alone as the One worthy of worship.

questions.question: Why does the passage say absolute Divinity cannot have any partner?
questions.answer: Because if others shared in worship, it would go against the very meaning and purpose of true Divinity.

questions.question: Who are described as the aware and living fruits at the top of creation?
questions.answer: Human beings who worship and give thanks.

questions.question: Why might people wrongly turn away from their real object of worship?
questions.answer: Because Allah is unseen, so some people may forget Him quickly and become attached to other things.

questions.question: What would be wrong if something else made people feel deeply thankful in a way that pulled them away from Allah?
questions.answer: It would wrongly take worship away from the One who truly deserves it.

questions.question: Why does the Qur’an strongly reject shirk in this passage?
questions.answer: Because giving worship to others besides Allah opposes the truth of Allah’s sole right to be worshipped.

questions.question: What warning does the passage say the Qur’an gives to people who commit shirk?
questions.answer: It warns them of Hellfire.

questions.question: In the passage, what does “absolute Divinity” mean in a simple way?
questions.answer: It means Allah alone has the full right to be worshipped.

questions.question: How do different groups of people show this truth according to the passage?
questions.answer: They are naturally drawn to different forms of worship based on how they were created.

questions.question: Besides people, what other parts of creation are mentioned as showing worship?
questions.answer: Animals and even nonliving things are mentioned.

questions.question: How do the gifts in the universe affect people’s hearts?
questions.answer: They push people to be thankful, grateful, and full of praise.

questions.question: What kinds of signs from beyond the seen world are mentioned?
questions.answer: Spiritual experiences, revelation, and inspiration are mentioned.

questions.question: What do all these signs together prove?
questions.answer: They prove that one single Divinity rules and deserves worship.

questions.question: Why is sharing worship with others called impossible in this passage?
questions.answer: Because true Divinity does not allow anyone else to share that place.

questions.question: What special place do worshipping people have in the universe, according to the passage?
questions.answer: They are presented as the highest, aware result of creation.

questions.question: What bad result would happen if people were made to forget Allah and turn to others?
questions.answer: The purpose of worship would be spoiled and directed the wrong way.

questions.question: Based on the passage, what is one reason the Qur’an speaks so firmly against polytheism?
questions.answer: Because polytheism steals worship away from Allah alone.

questions.question: What truth is being explained in the marked passage?
questions.answer: The truth of Allah’s sole Divinity.

questions.question: What human response is connected to blessings in the universe?
questions.answer: People are moved to thank, praise, and worship.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the actions of living creatures and nonliving things?
questions.answer: Their actions and duties show a kind of worship through obedience to their created roles.

questions.question: What do all the spiritual signs mentioned in the passage point toward?
questions.answer: They point toward Allah alone.

questions.question: If Allah’s Divinity is real and complete, what cannot be accepted?
questions.answer: Any partner sharing in worship cannot be accepted.

questions.question: Why does the passage focus on conscious and living beings when speaking about worship?
questions.answer: Because they can knowingly respond with thanks and worship.

questions.question: What human weakness is hinted at when the passage says the true object of worship may be quickly forgotten?
questions.answer: People can forget Allah when they focus too much on what they can see.

questions.question: What does this passage teach about the danger of being too attached to created things?
questions.answer: Created things can distract people from worshipping Allah if they are treated as if they deserve what belongs only to Him.

questions.question: What is the connection between the truth of Divinity and the Qur’an’s warning to polytheists?
questions.answer: Since Allah alone deserves worship, the Qur’an strongly warns those who give that worship to others.

questions.question: What is the best summary of the whole passage in one sentence?
questions.answer: All kinds of worship, blessings, and spiritual signs show that only Allah deserves worship and no partner can share that right.

questions.question: According to the passage, what do people’s natural ways of worship show?
questions.answer: They show that worship is part of how people were made and that it belongs to Allah.

questions.question: What do the regular tasks of animals and nonliving things teach the reader?
questions.answer: They teach that all creation serves in an ordered way that reflects worship.

questions.question: How do blessings become a reason for worship?
questions.answer: They make people feel thankful and lead them to praise Allah.

questions.question: What do revelation and inspiration help prove in this passage?
questions.answer: They help prove that Allah alone is worthy of worship.

questions.question: What word best describes the passage’s teaching about worshipping Allah and no one else: optional, shared, or exclusive?
questions.answer: Exclusive.

questions.question: Why does the passage describe human beings as being on the highest branches of the tree of the universe?
questions.answer: To show that they are a high and important part of creation because they can worship with understanding.

questions.question: What problem would happen if others could win people’s worship away from Allah?
questions.answer: It would oppose the holy purpose of Divinity.

questions.question: Why does invisibility make this test harder for people?
questions.answer: Because some people may ignore or forget what they cannot see.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the Qur’an’s style when speaking against shirk?
questions.answer: It says the Qur’an rejects it again and again very strongly.

questions.question: What punishment is mentioned for those who persist in polytheism?
questions.answer: Hellfire is mentioned.

questions.question: What does the passage say is proven in a very clear way?
questions.answer: It says the reality and rule of one absolute Divinity are clearly proven.

questions.question: Name one kind of evidence from human life that supports this truth.
questions.answer: People’s natural turning to worship supports it.

questions.question: Name one kind of evidence from the rest of creation that supports this truth.
questions.answer: The way animals and even nonliving things carry out their duties supports it.

questions.question: Name one kind of evidence from spiritual matters that supports this truth.
questions.answer: Revelation and inspiration support it.

questions.question: How do gifts and blessings in the universe affect worship?
questions.answer: They stir hearts to gratitude and worship.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about worship directed to anyone besides Allah?
questions.answer: It is false and does not fit the truth of Divinity.

questions.question: Why are conscious beings so important in this argument?
questions.answer: Because they are the ones who can knowingly give thanks and worship.

questions.question: What would be the result if people were pulled toward false objects of worship?
questions.answer: They would forget Allah and direct their worship in the wrong place.

questions.question: What cause-and-effect idea appears near the end of the passage?
questions.answer: Since only Allah deserves worship, the Qur’an forcefully rejects shirk and warns against it.

questions.question: What lesson should a Muslim student take from this passage?
questions.answer: A Muslim should worship Allah alone and not let anything take that place in the heart.

questions.question: What is the title of the truth explained in the marked passage?
questions.answer: It is the First Truth: Absolute Divinity.

questions.question: What are four broad kinds of signs mentioned in the passage that point to Allah alone?
questions.answer: People’s natural worship, the service of other creatures, the blessings of the universe, and spiritual signs like revelation and inspiration.

questions.question: How is worship shown by creatures that are not human?
questions.answer: It is shown by the way they fulfill the jobs given to them.

questions.question: How do the blessings of the world guide people toward Allah?
questions.answer: They encourage people to be thankful and to worship Him.

questions.question: What do all the signs from the unseen agree about?
questions.answer: They agree that worship belongs only to Allah.

questions.question: Why can true Divinity not be shared with anyone else?
questions.answer: Because the right to be worshipped belongs fully to Allah alone.

questions.question: In the passage, why are humans compared to the fruits on the highest branches?
questions.answer: Because they are conscious beings who can respond with thankful worship.

questions.question: What harmful change would happen if other things captured people’s worship?
questions.answer: People would turn away from Allah and forget the One they should worship.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention that Allah is unseen?
questions.answer: To explain why some people may be tempted to forget Him and become distracted by visible things.

questions.question: How does the passage explain the Qur’an’s repeated warnings against polytheism?
questions.answer: It explains that shirk is strongly condemned because it goes against Allah’s unique right to be worshipped.
